sections: Title/byline/abstract, graphical abstract and Introduction; distinguish cited spinel uses/claims from new synthesis data.
Introduction and literature crystal structures, complete Figure 1 and Figure 2; Zn-only PDF peak/model discussion.
Precursor protonation and mixed/alkaline solution discussion; Figures 3-5 and their captions/model limitations; Figure 4b legend conflict.
All 37 Table 1 rows, all five data columns and nomenclature footnote; in situ outcomes; Figure 6 and seconds/minutes conflict.
In situ phase/size discussion and Figure 7; laboratory microwave outcomes and Figures 8-9, all phase-fraction ESDs.
Microwave/SCF/autoclave comparisons, Figures 10-12, all quantitative fractions/bimodal sizes and color/sample conflicts.
Figure 13, literature band-gap ranges, conclusions with conflicting size and M/OH claims; reagents/workup/microwave stock and vessels.
Both literal heating profiles; SCF/ACS/in situ recipes, defect formula, all XRD/PDF/TEM/optical acquisition/refinement methods.
Optical-method ending; Supporting Information declaration, author/acknowledgment notes and references 1-20.
References continued, 21-56; cited studies retained as references only, not newly read source evidence.
References 57-65 and footer; complete supplied-main scope, with no local SI read or inferred.

items.title: Distinct formulations and precursor structures
items.text: The laboratory microwave/autoclave feed uses nitrate hydrates in demineralized water. The in situ nitrate experiments use a separate concentrated stock, while I15/I16 start from ZnO and Al(OH)3 in Millipore water. D1-D4 are precursor-solution scattering contexts. Water grades, nitrate hydration, ethanol grades, whole-stock charges and reaction aliquots remain distinct. The PDF interpretations identify coordination motifs without resolving every protonation state or solution species.

items.title: Zn-only precursor PDF
items.text: The Zn-only solution shows four strong short-range peaks below 3 Å; nitrate N-O is assigned at 1.2 Å and Zn-O near 2.0 Å. The source compares tetrahedral and octahedral reference distances and favors octahedral Zn-aquo monomers. The background reference to octahedral Zn in ZnAl2O4 is not silently substituted for the normal-spinel description.

items.title: Three laboratory routes and separate in situ experiments
items.text: Microwave, supercritical-flow and autoclave syntheses explore different thermal histories and metal-to-hydroxide conditions. Their products undergo the common powder workup separately. The full Table 1 matrix and both microwave heating profiles are retained, including conflicting total times, the S2 temperature discrepancy and the long-autoclave duration difference. In situ reaction monitoring and D-series scattering remain separately identified procedures.

items.title: Common laboratory powder workup
items.text: Separate as-synthesized powders from supernatant by centrifugation until the solution appears colorless. Wash the retained powders three times with demineralized water and once with 96% ethanol, then dry in a Thermo Scientific Heraeus vacuum oven. Centrifuge settings, solvent quantities, vacuum pressure and yields are absent. Apply this workup separately to the microwave, SCF and autoclave powders; these are alternative specimens, never a pooled charge. This workup is not automatically assigned to D-series solutions or in situ capillary observations.

items.title: In situ crystallite-size trajectories
items.text: Spherical-domain refinements generally start at 2.5-3.5 nm and reach 3.5-7 nm; I12/I13 are around 15 nm. Higher temperature increases size without impurities, while impurity-mediated cases show complex trends. The author nucleation/depletion interpretation is not an independently measured growth law.

notes: The complete supplied 11-page main extraction passed distinct source audit. Declared SI remains locally unlocated/unverified. Canonical/reader independent review remains pending; this is an unapproved private author draft. Historical pending flags in immutable source payloads refer to their author-freeze time.
Record IDs and context counts do not count independent physical batches or replicates.
No atomic model, exact recipe–structure pair, universal cross-technique sample join or training admission is approved.
Pure process specifications and author refinement/model results are distinguished from experimental product observations.
C4: Figure 6 axes print Time(s), while caption/prose describe an increase after about 34 min and Table 1 gives minutes.
C11: The text says two experiments (I12-I14), while Table 1 has three rows at 450, 475 and 400 °C. Do not assign high-temperature outcomes to I14 by range shorthand.
C9: M2 is called phase-pure but a tiny AlOOH peak is reported below reliable quantification. Preserve detection versus quantification limits.
C2: Methods say 450 °C for each synthesis; S2 is 380 °C in Table 1 and Results.
C3: Methods say 2.5 weeks; Table 1/Results use 17 days. Retain both without equating exact durations.
C6: Caption says green AlOOH/orange ZnO; plotted sample assignments and text identify green A3/A6 as ZnO and orange A4/A5 as AlOOH.
C8: Summary 2-42 nm conflicts with explicit A2 52.4(6) nm and A1 90.4(1) nm populations.

C12: Triangle/star/hexagon assignments place A1/A2 at about 1 day and A4/A5 at 17 days, whereas Table 1 and prose assign A1/A2 to 17 days and A4/A5 to 1 day. Preserve all source representations without relabeling the original graphic.

C13: Main p5 includes I4-I8 in initially phase-pure examples, while p4 describes the 1:2:7.81/1:2:8.34 mixtures as initially ZnO-bearing. I7/I8 are the 1:2:7.81 rows; unavailable SI prevents further reconciliation.

items.title: Coordination and impurity-mediated formation
items.text: The authors propose that aluminum dimers can connect with tetrahedrally coordinated zinc to nucleate spinel. At high M/OH, zinc recoordination may delay this process and favor AlOOH; at low M/OH, ZnO dissolution supplies zinc and may leave residual ZnO. Heating history changes impurity formation and consumption. These explanations are source interpretations, with the contradictory conclusion wording preserved.

items.text: Isotropic ADPs vary independently and become high; the authors attribute this to limited q-range, background, signal-to-noise and temperature. Antisite defects and interstitial Zn at (0,0,0) are refined under Zn/Al stoichiometry constraints. The complete refined values are in unavailable Table S7. items.title: Proposed nucleation pathways
items.text: High M/OH (lower pH) favors octahedral Zn monomers; their recoordination may limit tetrahedral-Zn spinel nucleation and permit AlOOH formation. Low M/OH (higher pH) favors ZnO as a tetrahedral-Zn reservoir, with dissolution feeding spinel and residual ZnO as impurity. This is an author mechanism, not directly measured rates or resolved molecular intermediates.
